events.label: founding
events.text: Town founded (as Enso) to serve a paper mill.

evidence.quote: the town was founded in 1887 to serve a paper mill

events.text: Moscow Peace Treaty ceded Enso to Soviet Union; border left factory on Soviet side.

evidence.quote: The territory was ceded by Finland to the Soviet Union by the Moscow Peace Treaty
In the 1940 Moscow Peace Treaty , the new Finnish-Soviet border was deliberately drawn

events.text: Enso became part of Yaskinsky District.

evidence.quote: In March 1940 , Enso became a part of Yaskinsky District

events.text: Finns recaptured Enso during the Continuation War (began).

evidence.quote: Enso was recaptured by Finns between 1941 and 1944

events.text: Finnish recapture ended; Enso ceded again to Soviets by Moscow Armistice.

evidence.quote: Enso was recaptured by Finns between 1941 and 1944

events.text: Yaskinsky District, including the town, transferred to Leningrad Oblast.

evidence.quote: On November 24 , 1944 , Yaskinsky District was transferred from Karelo-Finnish SSR to Leningrad Oblast

events.text: Paris Peace Treaty formalized Enso's secession to Soviet Union.

evidence.quote: This secession was formalized after signing the Paris Peace Treaty in 1947

events.text: Finnish place names replaced; Enso renamed Svetogorsk.

evidence.quote: on January 13 , 1949 , all Finnish names of the localities were replaced with Russian names

events.text: Lesogorsky District abolished and merged into Vyborgsky District.

evidence.quote: On December 9 , 1960 , Lesogorsky District was abolished and merged into Vyborgsky District

events.label: protest
events.text: About 500 residents protested with road barricade on Finnish-Russian border.

evidence.quote: On April 18 , 2008 , about five hundred inhabitants of Svetogorsk participated in a protest

undated_mentions: Border map redrawn so that it bends at Enso, after the Winter War (no date stated)
Sister city agreement with Imatra, Finland (no date stated)
